claims.text: An integrated DSC-ultrasonic-PVT approach can accurately determine melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across the high-entropy-alloy family.
The integrated approach can determine these properties efficiently.
Controlled atmospheres, calibrated heating rates, and calibrated pressure profiles minimize thermal gradients and compositional fluctuations.
Microstructural homogeneity and the absence of significant pre-melting segregation enable direct correlation of calorimetric signals, elastic moduli, and volumetric changes at melting.
DSC captures the latent heat associated with fusion.
DSC captures the melting temperature shift associated with fusion.
Ultrasonic measurements sensitive to changes in elastic moduli provide indirect measurements of density variations.
PVT measurements assess volume changes at melting and liquid-state behavior.
Correlating DSC and ultrasonic measurements with PVT data permits derivation of fusion enthalpy and entropy.
Correlating DSC and ultrasonic measurements with PVT data permits derivation of liquid-phase thermodynamic properties.
Combining the three techniques reduces systematic errors relative to standard single-method approaches.
The integrated approach will achieve approximately 2–3% uncertainty for melting-temperature measurements.
The integrated approach will achieve approximately 2–3% uncertainty for latent-heat measurements.
Standalone DSC measurements typically have uncertainties of 5–10%.
Traditional calorimetric or mechanical measurements performed independently have larger uncertainties and inefficiencies for HEAs.
The integrated approach is most applicable to HEAs that form stable single-phase solid solutions.
Secondary phases, segregation, eutectic compositions, or substantial intermetallic precipitation may diminish the accuracy of the integrated method.
Multielement interactions and metastable states may introduce unforeseen measurement errors.
Quantitative performance may vary significantly in HEAs with strong compositional inhomogeneity.

contradictions.description: The headline hypothesis claims accurate determination across the HEA family, whereas the predicted outcome and boundary restrict strongest expected performance to stable single-phase HEAs and acknowledge diminished accuracy for segregated or multiphase alloys.
